summary: The run reached Act 2 with a strong upgrade engine centered on Apotheosis, but the later deck decisions created a poor synergy between five Bites and Perfected Strike. The final combat then became unrecoverable after delaying use of the available Speed Potion and spending early turns on very low-impact actions while Spheric Guardian retained substantial Block. The most reusable improvements are to align event/card choices, use emergency resources before HP becomes critical, and continue prioritizing Apotheosis-like power upgrades.

lessons.title: Use emergency resources before the lethal range
lessons.situation: When facing a high-Block enemy that is attacking and your HP is already falling, especially when a potion is legally available.
lessons.lesson: Do not spend a turn on minimal mitigation and then end turn while holding an emergency potion. In the final fight, Speed Potion was available at 26 HP, but it was saved until 9 HP; at 9 HP, prioritize a line that immediately improves survival while also breaking through the enemy's Block.
evidence_points: Turn 3 began at 26/50 HP with 1 energy and Spheric Guardian at 49 Block; Defend was chosen for only 3 Block, followed by End turn, while Speed Potion was a legal alternative.
On Turn 4, the player was at 9/50 HP before using Speed Potion, then spent the turn on Iron Wave, Apotheosis+, Defend+, and Thunderclap+ without defeating the enemy.
On Turn 5, Spheric Guardian still had 20 HP and 21 Block after Burning Pact+, Perfected Strike+, and Thunderclap+.
lessons.reasoning: The log shows the potion was available during the safer state but was delayed until the player had only 9 HP. The subsequent actions reduced Block but did not create enough immediate damage or safety, leaving the player exposed to the next attack.

lessons.title: Keep Strike-dependent cards aligned with the Bite event
lessons.situation: When considering the event that removes all Strikes and grants five Bites, or when selecting cards whose scaling depends on the number of Strikes.
lessons.lesson: If accepting the Bite event, avoid taking Perfected Strike afterward—or refuse the event if Perfected Strike is already an important damage plan. The final deck should not simultaneously spend five slots on Bites, remove all Strikes, and retain a Strike-scaling attack with almost no supporting cards.
evidence_points: Act 2 Floor 18 selected Perfected Strike, then Act 2 Floor 19 accepted removal of all Strikes and received five Bites.
The final 25-card deck contains five Bites, one Perfected Strike, and no Strike cards.
The final combat included Perfected Strike+ against Spheric Guardian, but the enemy still had 21 Block afterward.
lessons.reasoning: The event and the later card choice pull the deck in opposite directions: Bites replace the Strikes that Perfected Strike wants to count. This left a large portion of the deck devoted to Bites while the remaining Perfected Strike had little permanent synergy.

lessons.title: Repeat the Apotheosis purchase-and-upgrade pattern
lessons.situation: When Apotheosis is available at a shop and there is enough gold to buy it without sacrificing an essential immediate survival resource.
lessons.lesson: Continue prioritizing Apotheosis over minor incremental purchases, then upgrade or preserve it as a central combat setup card. This run's purchase and later upgrade produced broad value across the remaining fights.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 11, Apotheosis was purchased for 192 gold when the player had 58/72 HP.
At Act 1 Floor 15, Apotheosis was upgraded at the rest site.
Apotheosis was used in the Guardian fight and again in the final Spheric Guardian fight, where Apotheosis+ upgraded the remaining hand.
lessons.reasoning: Unlike a narrow attack addition, Apotheosis improved many cards at once and was repeatedly used in important combats. The trajectory supports preserving this type of high-leverage upgrade plan in future runs.
